name: Swan Hill River Walk
bio_draft: 4.5 km riverside walk along the Murray from the Pump Station past the town's attractions.

facts.claim: 4.5 km walking trail along the Murray starting at the Pump Station, Milloo Street, passing many of the town's attractions
Easy walk ending north of Pental Island Bridge, around two hours

name: Lake Boga Flying Boat Museum
bio_draft: Restored Catalina flying boat and wartime exhibits at the former RAAF depot, 16 km from Swan Hill.

facts.claim: Museum on the shores of Lake Boga, between Swan Hill and Kerang, telling the story of the secret No. 1 Flying Boat Repair Depot (1942-1947)
Heritage-listed Catalina flying boat and original underground communications bunker are at the heart of the museum
About 500 artefacts on display plus interactive displays and personal stories

name: Shepparton Art Museum
bio_draft: Regional gallery in Shepparton with Australian and contemporary art.

facts.claim: Art museum at 530 Wyndham St, Shepparton; the current $50 million building opened in November 2021
Holds over 4,000 artworks, including one of Australia's largest ceramic collections and works by the Namatjira family
Entry is free, though certain exhibitions may be ticketed

facts.claim: Adventure playground at 7287 Midland Highway, Mooroopna, between Shepparton and Mooroopna
Entry is by gold coin donation; the miniature train costs extra

Multiple loop options for walking or cycling, including the Rail Trail to Wahgunyah beside the Murray, north to All Saints Winery and south to Lake Moodemere Estate

Originally opened by Victorian Railways in 1900 and now run as a tourist railway
Lakeside station has a visitor centre with a cafe, gift shop and a gallery of steam artefacts

name: Dandenong Ranges National Park

facts.claim: Forested volcanic hills covered in Mountain Ash, the world's tallest flowering tree, a short drive or train ride from Melbourne
Home to wallabies, lyrebirds, wombats and the Powerful Owl
Includes the 1000 Steps (Kokoda Track Memorial Walk) from Ferntree Gully Picnic Area, plus Olinda Falls and Sherbrooke Falls
The whole park closes on days of Extreme or higher Fire Danger Rating

name: Sherbrooke Forest

facts.claim: Cool temperate rainforest section of Dandenong Ranges National Park with a creek-fed gully at Sherbrooke Falls
Sherbrooke Falls walk and Sherbrooke picnic ground are the main visitor points; falls are best after rain
Park closes on Extreme or higher fire danger days

name: William Ricketts Sanctuary

facts.claim: Forest sanctuary on Mount Dandenong with 92 ceramic sculptures by William Ricketts set among fern gullies and rock faces
Reopened its first stage on 3 August 2026 after being closed since a June 2021 storm; some areas remain closed for restoration
An audio tour can be hired at the sanctuary for $5
Managed by Parks Victoria as a heritage site

name: National Rhododendron Gardens

facts.claim: Now called Dandenong Ranges Botanic Garden (formerly the National Rhododendron Garden), a 50 hectare cool-climate garden at Olinda with views over the Yarra Valley
Holds over 15,000 rhododendrons, 12,000 azaleas, 3,000 camellias and 250,000 daffodils, in flower in spring and autumn
A 3.5 km paved circuit passes a pond and ornamental lake; the site also has a re-created Chelsea Flower Show Australian Garden and a 101 hectare arboretum

Gateway to Olinda Falls and the national park forest walks, and next to the Dandenong Ranges Botanic Garden

Easy and moderate walks start here, including the 82 Rose Steps up the dam wall
The dam and reservoir (1927) are part of the heritage-listed Maroondah Water Supply System
Access to the surrounding protected water catchment is prohibited; only the park, limited walking tracks and the aqueduct walk are open

name: Badger Weir

Three easy nature walks lead from the picnic ground to Badger Creek: Coranderrk Track (1.1 km, flat, stroller friendly), Slip Creek Track (1.4 km) and Lyrebird Track (1.1 km)
Fungi appear in autumn and winter and the creek is good for cooling off in summer
